title: Does increased sunlight exposure work as a strategy to improve vitamin D status in the elderly: a cluster randomised controlled trial
authors: Sambrook PN, Cameron ID, Chen JS, Cumming RG, Durvasula S, Herrmann M, et al.
population: Residents aged 70 years or older (mean 86.4 years, 71% women) of 51 aged care facilities in Northern Sydney, Australia; median baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D 32.9 nmol/L
funder: The full text was not accessible. Registry: lead sponsor University of Sydney; no collaborators listed. The publication's funding statement was not read.
result: Cluster randomisation by facility to additional sunlight exposure of 30 to 40 minutes a day in the early morning, with or without calcium 600 mg/day, or neither, for a year. Median adherence to sunlight sessions was 26% (IQR 7% to 45%); 25-hydroxyvitamin D increased only slightly with the number of sessions attended. Falls: 327 in 111 (54%) control participants, 326 in 111 (58%) with UV only and 335 in 108 (52%) with UV plus calcium; intention-to-treat IRR for increased UV exposure 1.06 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.48). In 66 participants attending 130 or more sessions a year, falls were lower (IRR 0.52, 0.31 to 0.88), a non-randomised comparison.
